title: A governed Core parameter in the Compound Instance contains an unfinished sentence instead of a value
content:
The prospective Compound Integration Boost Instance specifies its Data Submission Responsible Actor as: "The Data Submission Responsible Actor is The Data Submission Responsible Actor is." (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.4.1.2.6). The template's lead-in has been duplicated and no actor named.

Every other Instance of this primitive fills the same field with "Core Council Risk Advisor", so the intended value is inferable — but the document as published names nobody, in a `[Core]` parameter that determines who produces the numbers the boost is calculated from.

The finding is not the typo itself but what it implies about the pipeline. These are structured, addressable, UUID-bearing documents inside a governance framework whose integrity claims rest on that structure — yet a required field can hold a fragment of its own template and still ship. No schema check, no required-value validation, and no reviewer caught it.

That matters more here than in ordinary prose because of how the Atlas is meant to be read: as machine-navigable state where the value at an address *is* the rule. Downstream automation reading this field gets a sentence, not an actor. The Instance is at `Planning` status, so nothing is presently paid on the strength of it — which is likely why it survived — but the same class of defect in an Active Instance would be a live governance hazard rather than an untidy draft.
